title: Find The Duck
story: The office rubber duck has gone missing.
Engineering cannot debug anything without explaining it to the duck first.
Three deploys have failed. Morale is low. Someone is crying in the server room.
Find the duck. The duck knows the code.
objective: Find the rubber duck and submit the code it is guarding.

files./office/lobby/sign.txt: WELCOME TO DEADPORT. PLEASE DO NOT FEED THE INTERNS.
/office/floor1/supply_closet/duck_tape.t: Bob labelled it 'duck tape'. It is not a duck.
Please stop opening this file looking for the duck.
files./office/floor1/supply_closet/staplers.tx: There are 41 staplers. Nobody has ever seen a staple.
files./office/floor2/desk_14/drawer.txt: A single sock and a USB stick labelled 'DO NOT PLUG IN'. Someone has plugged it in.
files./office/floor2/desk_15/drawer.txt: Seventeen ketchup packets and a resignation letter dated 2014. Still employed.
files./office/floor3/breakroom/microwave.txt: Someone microwaved fish. HR has been notified. HR has resigned.
files./office/floor3/breakroom/fridge/milk.txt: Expired. Sentient. Has opinions about tabs versus spaces.
/office/floor3/breakroom/fridge/.yogurt_: You found the duck. It was cold.
files./office/floor3/server_room/README.txt: It's hot in here. Please don't put the duck in here.

hints: The duck is not in a place anyone would look on purpose.
find can search by name: find /office -name "*duck*"
Hidden folders start with a dot. Have you checked the fridge with ls -a?
completion: The duck has been returned to Engineering.
Deploys are succeeding again. Nobody can explain why.
The duck can. The duck won't.
